sections.title: Getting Your Computer Ready
sections.lede: Jack introduces Level 0: eight short videos that make sure your computer is ready to run your agent.
words: Hi, I'm Jack. I help build Archie. Archie is an app that runs your AI helper, called an agent.
First, let's make sure your computer is ready. Each video is short. Skip any topic you already know.

sections.title: Will Archie Work on My Computer?
sections.lede: Archie runs on a Mac or a Windows computer. How to tell which one you have, and what else it needs.
sections.notes_heading: Which Macs and Windows computers run Archie
notes: Mac: macOS 12 Monterey or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.
Windows: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
Download Archie from its install page, which lists the rest of what it needs.
words: Will Archie work on the computer I have?
Archie runs on a Mac or a Windows computer. Your agent cannot run on a Chromebook, an iPad, or a phone. You can use your phone to talk to it later, but the agent runs on your computer.
Not sure which computer you have? A Mac has an Apple logo and an Apple menu in the top corner of the screen. A Windows computer has a Start button on the bar along the bottom.
Your computer needs a supported version of its system software. Check the list below this video to see which versions work.
It also needs a steady internet connection and a place where it can stay plugged in and turned on.
A laptop can work. A desktop may be easier because it usually stays in one place.
Next: why your computer needs to stay on.

sections.title: Why Your Computer Needs to Stay On
sections.lede: Your agent works only while the computer is on, awake and running Archie. How to keep it that way.
sections.notes_heading: How to keep a Mac or Windows computer awake while it is plugged in
notes: On a Mac, open System Settings, then Battery, then Options, and turn on Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off. On a desktop Mac, it is under Energy Saver.
On Windows, open Settings, then System, then Power & battery, and under Screen and sleep set sleep when plugged in to Never.
Closing Archie’s window switches your agent off, the same as quitting. Minimize the window instead.
words: Why does my computer need to stay on?
Your agent runs on your computer. To read your messages and write its replies, it connects to an AI company over the internet. The rest of the work happens on your computer.
Your agent can work only while your computer is on, awake, and running Archie. Awake means the computer is not in sleep mode.
If the computer is off or asleep, your agent cannot check your email or send reminders on time. Archie can wake a sleeping computer for a routine. The next video tells you more.
Choose a computer that can stay plugged in. Change its settings so it does not go to sleep while plugged in. The steps for Mac and Windows are below this video.
The screen can go dark while the computer stays awake.
Keep Archie open, too. Closing its window stops your agent. Minimize the window instead. That hides the window without closing Archie.
Next: what sleep, shut down, and restart mean.

sections.title: What Sleep, Shut Down, and Restart Mean
sections.lede: What sleep, shut down and restart each do to your agent, and how Archie can wake the computer for a routine.
sections.notes_heading: How to set up Archie to wake your computer for a routine
notes: On a Mac, setting it up asks for your password once, because only an administrator of a Mac may schedule a wake. The Mac asks for it in its own box: Archie never sees what you type.

On Windows, setting it up is one press. Windows lets you schedule a wake for your own computer, so there is nothing to approve. On some laptops the power plan has to allow wake timers, and the Routines card names the presses that change it.
Archie wakes a sleeping computer. A computer that is shut down stays shut down.
To open Archie when you sign in: Settings, then How Archie looks and opens, then Open Archie at login. It starts off.
words: What happens to my agent when my computer sleeps, shuts down, or restarts?
Sleep puts your computer on pause. Your agent pauses, too. It cannot read or answer messages while the computer sleeps. A message sent during that time may never get a reply.
Archie can wake your computer for a routine. A routine is a task set to run at a certain time, such as a summary at seven each morning. After the task, the computer can go back to sleep.
This needs a one-time setup. Some Windows laptops also need a power setting changed. The steps are below this video.
Shut down turns your computer off. Your agent stops, and someone must turn the computer back on.
Restart turns your computer off and back on. You may do this after an update. Your agent can work again after you sign in and open Archie.
Archie can open when you sign in. In Settings, turn on Open Archie at login. This setting starts off.
For regular use, keep your computer plugged in and awake, with Archie open.
Next: how to download and install an app.

sections.title: How to Download and Install an App
sections.lede: The difference between downloading an app and installing it, and where to get apps safely.
sections.notes_heading: Where to download Archie
notes: Archie’s own download page is otianai.com/archie/install. Type the address into your browser yourself.
words: What is the difference between downloading and installing?
An app is a tool you use on your computer, such as a calculator or a web browser.
Downloading saves the app's setup file to your computer. It usually goes into a folder called Downloads. Think of it as a package arriving at your door.
Installing gets the app ready to use. Open the file you downloaded and follow the steps on the screen. This is like unpacking the package.
When you finish, you can open the app from its icon.
Get apps from the company's own website or an official app store. Type the website address into your browser yourself.
Skip download links sent by strangers or shown in ads.
Next: why your computer asks for permission.

sections.title: Why Your Computer Asks for Permission
sections.lede: Why your computer asks before it opens an app or lets one use your files, and how to tell a normal question from one to refuse.
sections.notes_heading: What Windows shows the first time you open Archie
notes: Windows shows a box that says Windows protected your PC. The install page shows it and says what to check before you continue.
words: Why does my computer keep asking if I'm sure?
Your computer may ask before it opens a new app. It may also ask before an app uses your files, camera, or microphone.
Read the message before you answer. Check the app's name and what it wants to do.
Does it name the app you chose to install from the company's website? That can be a normal part of setup.
Does it name something you do not recognize? Did it appear when you were doing something else? Choose No.
Your computer cannot know which website you meant to use. You still need to check the website and the name in the message.
Next: where your passwords and account keys are stored.

sections.title: Where Your Passwords and Account Keys Are Stored
sections.lede: Where Archie keeps the keys that reach your accounts: your computer’s own password store, which Otian cannot read.
words: Where does Archie keep the codes it uses to reach my accounts?

Your computer has a built-in place for passwords. Think of it as a locked safe. On a Mac, it is called Keychain. On Windows, it is called Credential Manager. It opens with the password you use to sign in to your computer.
An app may use a special code, called a key, to connect to an account. Archie keeps your AI key and the keys for your connected accounts in this password store.
Otian, the company behind Archie, cannot read the keys stored there. When your agent uses a key, Archie sends it only to the company that key belongs to.
This is one reason your computer's password matters. Choose one that is hard to guess, and do not share it.
Next: what it means to connect an account.

sections.title: What It Means to Connect an Account
sections.lede: What you agree to when you connect your email, how to take that access back, and why connecting sends nothing.
sections.notes_heading: What Google shows first, and where to take access back
notes: Until Google verifies Archie, connecting a Google account first shows a screen saying Google hasn’t verified this app. It names Otian AI, the company that makes Archie.
To go on, press Advanced, then the link to Otian AI, which Google marks unsafe until it has verified the app.
Google: myaccount.google.com/permissions.
Microsoft: account.microsoft.com, under the apps you have given access.
Apple: an app-specific password is cancelled at account.apple.com, under Sign-In and Security.
words: What am I agreeing to when I connect my email?
For a Google or Microsoft account, the company's own sign-in page opens. It asks what you will allow Archie to access, such as your email or calendar.
Think of this as giving Archie a key card. The card opens certain doors. It does not give Archie your Google or Microsoft password.
Read the list before you agree. You can say no, and nothing changes.
You can also remove access later in your Google or Microsoft account settings. You can do this even after removing Archie from your computer.
Some services, such as iCloud, work differently. You make a separate app password on that service's website and paste it into Archie. You can cancel that password there later.
Connecting your email does not mean Archie starts sending replies. There is a separate switch for that.
Even with the switch on, a reply waits until you send it or choose a time for it to be sent.
Next: how to talk to your agent from your phone.

sections.title: Talking to Your Agent From Your Phone
sections.lede: How to message your agent from a chat app on your phone, and the path each message takes.
sections.notes_heading: The chat apps Archie works with
notes: Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, and on a Mac, iMessage, in the thread you have with yourself.
Archie does not connect to WhatsApp.
words: How do I talk to my agent when I am away from my computer?
You can send it a message in a chat app, such as Telegram. On a Mac, your agent can also reply in the iMessage chat you have with yourself.
You can chat inside Archie, too. The full list of supported chat apps is below this video.
Try a message such as, "Remind me about the water bill on Friday." Your agent answers in the same chat.
Your message passes through the chat company's computers, then reaches the computer running your agent. The reply comes back the same way.
The chat company carries these messages, just as it carries other messages sent through its app.
You connect the chat app once. For Telegram, you first create a bot, a special chat contact for your agent. Then you send that bot the code Archie gives you. The setup video shows each step.
That is the end of Level 0. Next: the basics of AI.

sections.title: What AI Is and Is Not
sections.lede: What AI is, where you already use it, and what it cannot know about you.
sections.notes_heading: More AI words, in plain English
notes: AI Explained, our glossary, defines each one in a sentence or two.
words: What is AI?
AI stands for artificial intelligence. You may already use it when your phone fixes a spelling mistake, your email filters out junk mail, or your map app picks a route.

Tools such as ChatGPT and Claude are a newer kind of AI. They learned patterns from a very large amount of writing. These patterns include how people answer questions, write emails, and connect ideas.
When you ask a question, the AI uses those patterns to write an answer. The answer can be useful, but it can also be wrong.
AI is not a person. It does not have feelings. It does not know about your life unless you give it that information.
Next: why AI sometimes gets things wrong.

sections.title: Why AI Sometimes Gets Things Wrong
sections.lede: Why AI sometimes writes something wrong and sounds sure of it, and three habits that catch it.
sections.notes_heading: Hallucination, in plain English
notes: The AI Explained entry for hallucination.
words: Why does AI get things wrong?
AI uses patterns to write answers. Sometimes it gives the right answer. Other times, it fills in a detail that is wrong or made up.
It might give you the wrong date or include a fact that is not true. People call this a hallucination.
The hard part is that AI can sound sure of itself even when it is wrong.
Three habits can help you catch mistakes.
First, read anything before you send it.
Second, check important names, numbers, and dates.
Third, ask where an answer came from when something seems surprising.
For example, if your agent used a PDF you shared, it can tell you the page number. You can open that page and check.
Archie also reminds you to check answers before you act on them. Replies and calendar changes wait for your approval.
You make the final decision.
Next: how to ask AI for what you need.

sections.title: What a Prompt Is
sections.lede: What a prompt is, and how saying who, what and how gets you a better answer.
sections.notes_heading: Prompt, in plain English
notes: The AI Explained entry for prompt.
words: What is a prompt?
A prompt is a message or question you give to AI. You can type it or say it. You do not need special words.
It helps to explain what you need. Compare these two requests.
"Write an email."
"Write a short, friendly email to my landlord. Ask if someone can fix the sink this week."
The second request tells the AI who the email is for, what it should say, and how it should sound.
You can also ask for changes. Try "Make it shorter" or "Make it more polite."
You do not have to get the first request perfect.
Next: what AI remembers.

sections.title: What AI Remembers
sections.lede: What AI keeps from one chat to the next, and the notes your agent keeps about you.
sections.notes_heading: Context window, in plain English
notes: The AI Explained entry for context window.
words: Does AI remember what I told it?
AI uses information from the chat you are having now. This information is called context.
There is a limit to how much it can use at once. In a long chat, the oldest messages may no longer be available to it. A new chat does not bring over the whole old conversation.
Your agent also keeps a short list of things it has learned about you. This is separate from the chat itself.
You can read that list on your agent's Knowledge tab. You can add a note or delete one, too.
Your agent uses recent notes. Older notes can come back when the words in your message match them.
It still cannot know a decision you never shared. For example, if you cancel a subscription but never tell it, it does not know about that decision.
Next: the difference between a chatbot and an agent.

sections.title: Chatbot or Agent: What Is the Difference?
sections.lede: How a chatbot and an agent differ, and why replies and calendar moves wait for your yes in Archie.
sections.notes_heading: Chatbot and agent, in plain English
notes: The AI Explained entries for chatbot and AI agent.
words: What is the difference between a chatbot and an agent?
A chatbot gives you an answer. Ask it to write an email to your landlord, and it gives you the words. You then open your email, copy in the message, and send it.
An agent can help with the steps, too. It can read your landlord's email, write a reply, and show it to you ready to send.
It can also work on a schedule, such as checking each morning for bills that are due.
To help with these tasks, it needs your permission to connect to accounts such as your email and calendar.
With Archie, you choose when a reply is sent. Calendar changes also need your approval.
Next: the companies that provide the AI.

sections.title: Where Archie Gets Its AI
sections.lede: Which companies build the AI Archie uses, how you pick one, and where the free credits send your messages.
sections.notes_heading: The seven AI companies Archie works with
notes: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, xAI, DeepSeek and Mistral. Another provider, the eighth choice, is for any service that works like OpenAI’s.
What each company says about training on what you send, in its own words: the Trust page.
words: Does Archie make its own AI?
No. Other companies build the AI models. An AI model is the technology that puts together an answer. Anthropic makes Claude, OpenAI makes ChatGPT, and Google makes Gemini. These are a few examples.
Archie is the app that runs your agent on your computer. Your agent uses your routines, lists, and connected accounts.
To read your messages and write its replies, it uses the AI company you chose. You can change that choice later.
The companies charge different prices. They also have different rules for how they handle the information you send them.
Our Trust page shows what each company says about using what you send to train its AI. Read it before you choose.
When you use our free credits, your agent uses Claude through our Anthropic account, so your messages pass through our server on the way.
Next: why using AI costs money.

sections.title: Why Using AI Costs Money
sections.lede: What tokens are, why AI companies charge for them, and what makes a month cost more.
sections.notes_heading: Tokens, and what a month costs
notes: The AI Explained entry for token.
Three example months, measured: 1.10 and the pricing page.
words: Why does using AI cost money?
Writing an AI answer uses big computers in large data centers. The AI company charges for that work.
It measures the amount of text in small pieces called tokens. A token can be part of a word. The company counts both the information sent to the AI and the answer it writes back.
A short task, such as writing a two-line reply, usually uses fewer tokens. A longer task, such as summarizing many documents, uses more.
Tasks that run on a schedule count, too, even when you are asleep.
Your monthly cost depends on how much work your agent does. We measured example months to show what that can look like. The results are below this video and in the cost video later in this level.
Next: why your ChatGPT subscription does not pay for Archie to use AI.

sections.title: Why Your ChatGPT Plan Does Not Cover Archie
sections.lede: Why a ChatGPT or Claude subscription cannot run Archie, and the three ways to give your agent its AI.
sections.notes_heading: Your three choices, and what each costs
notes: Free credits: no card needed. They last 14 days or until they are spent, whichever comes first.
An AI account of your own, with no plan: Archie is free for 20 jobs a day. A job is one piece of work: a reply to you, a routine running, or an email it reacts to.
A plan: $30 a month or $299 a year.
A plan with the AI included: $59 a month or $599 a year, with $25 of Claude use each month.
That $25 refills each paid month and nothing carries over. When it is used up, your agent pauses until the next month, or until you connect an AI account of your own.
Email features and the text watch need an AI account of your own. The free starter credits and the plan with the AI included will not run them.
words: I already pay for ChatGPT. Can Archie use that plan?
No. Archie cannot use a ChatGPT or Claude subscription.
Archie needs a different way to use the company's AI. This is called a pay-as-you-go account. You may also see it called a developer account or an API account.
It has its own setup and its own bill. Your chat subscription does not cover it.
You have three main choices for using AI with Archie.
You can try our free credits. You do not need a payment card.
You can connect your own pay-as-you-go AI account. With your own account, Archie is free, with a daily limit on jobs. A job is one task your agent runs. The current limit is below this video.

Or you can choose a plan with some AI use included each month. When that runs out, your agent pauses until the next month. Some jobs, like reading your email, need your own AI account. The list below this video says which.
Next: how to open your own AI account.

sections.title: How to Open Your AI Account
sections.lede: Step by step: open an Anthropic account, buy credit, and make the key Archie needs.
sections.hold: The narration promises the key's choices below the video, and which to pick is not tested yet (a key tied to no workspace may be refused).
sections.notes_heading: The Claude Console, and the choices to make in it
notes: The Claude Console: API keys and billing.
Auto-reload is on the billing page. Off means your agent stops when the credit runs out, until you add more. When that happens, your agent says so in the chat, with the billing link.
Archie has a guide like this one for each of the other six companies, and for Another provider.
words: Let's open your AI account. Have your email address and a payment card ready.
This example uses Anthropic, the company that makes Claude. Our free credits use Claude, and our cost examples were measured with it. Archie has separate guides for the other AI companies.
Step one. Open the Claude Console using the link below. This is Anthropic's developer website. It is separate from the Claude chat app, so check the address.
Step two. Sign in, or create an account with your email address. If you made a new account, open the confirmation email and follow its instructions.
Step three. Open billing, add a payment card, and buy some credit.
You will see an option called auto-reload. It buys more credit when your balance runs low.
Leave it off to stop buying more credit automatically. When your credit runs out, your agent stops working and tells you how to add more.
Turn it on to let the account buy more credit for you. You can change this choice later.
Step four. Open API keys and make a new key named Archie. The list below this video shows which choices to pick. A key is a private code that lets Archie use your AI account.
When you are asked when the key should expire, choose Never. This helps avoid your agent stopping because the key has expired.
Step five. Copy the key into Archie when asked. Archie checks whether it works.
Keep this key private, like a password. Do not email it or share it.
Next: what a month of AI use may cost.

sections.title: What a Month of AI Use May Cost
sections.lede: Three example months of AI use, measured, and the two things that move your bill most.
sections.notes_heading: What three example months cost, measured
notes: AI cost for one agent, per month, at Anthropic’s prices of September 12, 2026. Economy and Balanced are Archie’s two quality settings.
Light, a calendar and a folder, about 6 messages a day: $1 to $2 at Economy, $2 to $5 at Balanced.
Moderate, calendar and inbox, about 25 messages and 80 emails a day: $21 to $42 at Economy, $22 to $41 at Balanced.
Heavy, everything connected, about 70 messages and 200 emails a day: $64 to $132 at Economy, $69 to $139 at Balanced.
These are estimates. Your real bill is on your AI company’s own billing page. How they were measured: the pricing page.
words: How much will I pay for AI each month?
It depends on how much work your agent does. We measured three example months.
Light use means a connected calendar, a folder of documents, and a few messages each day.
Moderate use adds email and a to-do list, with more messages and a busy inbox.
Heavy use means using those connections and more throughout the day.
The measured cost for each example is below this video.
Two things affect your bill most: how much you use your agent and how much you connect to it. Scheduled tasks add to the total, too.
Choose whether your AI account buys more credit automatically. With that off, your agent stops when the credit runs out. With it on, the account buys more credit so your agent can keep working.
Archie's Account page shows an estimate of your AI spending for the month. Check the AI company's billing page for the actual bill.
That is the end of Level 1. Next: how your agent works.

sections.title: How Your Agent Works
sections.lede: Jack introduces Level 2: jobs, routines, add-ons, connected accounts, what waits for your approval, and what your agent cannot do.
words: Now let's look at how your agent works day to day. These five videos explain jobs, routines, add-ons, account connections, the changes that need your approval, and what your agent cannot do.

sections.title: Jobs and Routines
sections.lede: What a job is, the three ways one starts, and how a routine runs on a schedule.
sections.notes_heading: How many jobs a day Archie does for free
notes: On an AI account of your own with no plan, Archie does 20 jobs a day. Routines and the mail and text watches stop at 15, so the last 5 are kept for what you ask it yourself.
words: How does my agent know what to do?
Each task your agent does is called a job.
A job can start in three ways. You ask for something. A scheduled task is due to run. Or something arrives that your agent is set to watch for, such as a new email.
A request such as "Draft a reply to Sam" gives your agent a job to do once.
A routine is a task that runs on a schedule. For example, it might send your daily summary at seven each morning or tell you three days before a bill is due.
You do not need to ask again every time. The routine runs at the times you set.
Each time a routine runs, it counts as a job. Each run uses AI and adds to your AI cost.
Start with a few routines. Add more as you learn what helps you.
Your agent's Jobs tab lists the jobs it has run.
Next: how add-ons give your agent instructions for more tasks.

sections.title: How Add-ons Help Your Agent
sections.lede: What an add-on is, where to find more of them, and how your agent writes a new one only after you approve it.
sections.notes_heading: Every add-on in the Marketplace
notes: Archie’s Marketplace has 160 add-ons, and every one is included with Archie.
Browse every add-on on our website.
words: How does my agent learn to track bills or organize receipts?
It uses add-ons. An add-on is a set of written instructions for a task. Think of it as a recipe your agent follows.
For example, an add-on might explain how to track your subscriptions or watch for return deadlines.
Your agent starts with a few add-ons. You can find more in Archie's Marketplace. Every add-on is included with Archie.
An add-on is a text file your agent reads. It does not give your agent a way to run code or a command on your computer.
Not sure which add-on to choose? Ask your agent. It searches for one that fits your request.
If none fits, it can write new instructions, called a skill. It shows you what it plans to add and waits for your approval.
Next: connecting your email and calendar.

sections.title: Connecting Your Email and Calendar
sections.lede: How to connect a Google, Outlook or iCloud account in four steps, and how to take that access back.
sections.notes_heading: Which accounts connect, and what Google shows first
notes: Google and Outlook (Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live and Office 365) open their own sign-in page in your browser.
iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, AOL, Zoho Mail and GMX connect with an app password you make on that service’s website. A calendar connects when Archie finds one as you connect. AOL and GMX have none.
Until Google verifies Archie, connecting a Google account first shows a screen saying Google hasn’t verified this app. It names Otian AI, the company that makes Archie.
To go on, press Advanced, then the link to Otian AI, which Google marks unsafe until it has verified the app.
Email needs an AI account of your own. The free starter credits and the plan with the AI included will not run it.
Where to take access back at Google, Microsoft and Apple: 0.7.
words: Let's connect your email and calendar.
First, an important limit: your agent can read email only when you use your own AI account.
Email is off when you use our free credits or a plan with AI included. With those options, the emails other people sent you would pass through our server. They did not agree to that.
Step one. Open your agent in Archie. Go to Connections. Under Email, calendar, files, select Connect an account.
Step two. Choose your service, such as Google, Outlook, or iCloud. Before you press Google or Outlook, open Choose exactly what it may do. Find Let it send replies. This switch starts on.
Turn it off to let your agent write drafts for you to send yourself. Even when it is on, a reply waits until you send it or choose a time to send it.

Step three. For Google or Outlook, the company's sign-in page opens in your browser. It may name Otian AI, the company that makes Archie. Read the list of permissions before you agree. It tells you what Archie will be allowed to access. If a warning shows first, the list below this video says what to do.
For iCloud and some other services, create an app password on that service's website. Then paste it into Archie.
Step four. Return to Archie. Your account appears in the list. For most services, the calendar connects along with the account.
To remove an account later, select Remove, shown as a trash can beside the account.
You can also remove permission in your Google or Microsoft account settings.
Next: why Archie waits for your approval.

sections.title: The Approval Gate: Why Archie Waits for You
sections.lede: Why replies and calendar changes wait for your approval, and what a routine running at night does instead.
words: Will my agent send emails without asking me?
No. Replies and calendar changes need your approval.
Your agent can read your email and calendar and prepare a suggestion. An email reply appears as a card in your chat. You can send it, edit it, choose a time to send it, or dismiss it.
A calendar change also appears for you to review and approve.
Why does Archie wait? Your agent only has the information you have shared. It may not know about a decision you made or a detail you left out.
A routine running on its own at night cannot send a reply or change your calendar. It tells you what it would have done instead.
Read each card before you approve it. Approval only helps when you check the details.
There is no setting that turns this approval step off.
Next: the things your agent cannot do.

sections.title: What Your Agent Cannot Do
sections.lede: What your agent will not do on a website, how buying works if you switch it on, and how to stop your agent.
sections.notes_heading: Buying, and a hard limit on what your agent spends
notes: Buying is off until you switch it on, under Computer control on the Connections tab. When you do, the limit for one order starts at $50, and you can change it.
Your agent never types a card you pay with, so your card has to be saved at the shop already.
The limit is checked against the price your agent reads on the page. For a ceiling nobody can get past, use a card from your bank that works at one shop, with its own limit.
words: Are there things my agent cannot do?
Yes. Some limits are built into Archie.
Your agent cannot run code or a command on your computer. It cannot make a phone call or send a text on its own.
If you let it use websites, it will not type a password, a card you pay with, or a sign-in code. It stops and lets you take over.
You must handle bank transfers and contract signatures yourself. Do not ask your agent to do them.
Buying is off unless you turn it on. If you turn it on, you choose the stores it may buy from. You also set a limit for each order and a limit for each week or month.
Even with it turned on, your agent still asks before each order.
The spending check uses the price your agent reads on the page. If the store adds a charge at the last step, the final price can be higher than your limit.
For a hard limit, use a card from your bank that only works at one store and stops at an amount you pick.
These limits do not stop AI from making mistakes. You still need to review its drafts.
To stop your agent, quit Archie. There is nowhere else it is running.
That is the end of Level 2. Next: where your information goes.

sections.title: Privacy and Trust
sections.lede: Jack introduces Level 3: where your messages go, what information Otian keeps, and how to stop using Archie and keep what you built.
words: These three videos explain where your messages go, what information Otian keeps, and how to stop using Archie while keeping a copy of what you've built.

sections.title: Where Your Messages Go
sections.lede: The path a message takes from your phone to your computer, on to the AI company and back, and the two cases where it passes through our server.
sections.notes_heading: Every connection Archie makes
notes: The Trust page lists every connection Archie makes and what each one carries.
Our one server, for the free credits and the plan with the AI included, is archie-4f35.onrender.com.
words: Where does my message go when I talk to my agent?
Let's follow a message sent through Telegram.
First, it passes through Telegram's computers. These are called servers. Then it reaches your computer, where your agent runs.
When your agent needs AI help, it sends your words to the AI company you chose, such as Anthropic or OpenAI. If it searches the web, that search happens at the AI company, too.
The answer returns to your computer. Your agent sends the reply back through Telegram to your phone.
When you use your own AI account, the connection from your computer to the AI company goes directly to that company. Otian is not in the middle of that connection.
There are two cases where your messages pass through Otian's server.

First, when you use our free credits or a plan with AI included, your messages pass through our server on their way to Anthropic. We record the cost of each request. We do not keep a record of its contents or keep a copy.
Second, if you use the Archie phone app on an Android phone, messages between it and your computer wait on our server in a locked form. We never receive the key that opens them.
We can see when a message was left there, which version of Archie left it, and whether it was picked up, but we cannot read it. This phone access stays off unless you turn it on.
Next: what information Otian keeps.

sections.title: What Information Otian Keeps
sections.lede: What our servers keep about you, what they never hold, and the three reports Archie can send, which you can turn off.
sections.notes_heading: The full list, how long the phone mailbox keeps things, and how to check
notes: The complete list of what we hold.
The phone deletes a message once it has read it. One it never came back for is cleared by your computer a day after it was answered, the next time Archie is running.
The sealed picture of your agent that the phone shows is replaced as it changes, and removed when you press Disconnect every phone or delete your account.
You can check our claims yourself with a network monitor in about 10 minutes. The Trust page shows how.
words: What information does Otian keep about me?
Our servers keep your email address and whether you have a plan. We also keep which version of Archie you run, and reports about crashes and errors.
If you use the Archie phone app on an Android phone, we also hold the messages between your phone and computer, until you turn phone access off. Those messages are locked with a key we never receive.
We do not keep conversations in a form we can read. We do not keep your emails, calendar, or files.
Your account keys are stored in your computer's password store. We cannot read the keys stored there.
Archie does not use an analytics service, a service that tracks how people use an app.

It can send three kinds of reports: a check-in with your app version, a crash report, and an error report. These are linked to your account ID. They do not include anything you wrote, and you can turn them off in Settings.
Our Trust page has the full list. It also shows where Archie connects and how you can check those connections yourself.
Next: how to stop using Archie and save your work.

sections.title: How to Stop Using Archie and Save Your Work
sections.lede: Five steps, in order: save a backup, end your plan, take back account access, reset Archie, and remove the app.
sections.notes_heading: The last steps, and what Reset leaves behind
notes: A full refund within 14 days of first starting a plan, by email. Guided sessions are not refunded.
If you use the Archie phone app, press Disconnect every phone before you reset. It is on your agent’s Setup tab, under Chat app, on the Archie Mobile row.
Reset leaves the phone mailbox on our server, sealed, until you press Disconnect every phone or delete your account.

On a Mac, to leave nothing of Archie behind: after Reset, turn off Open Archie at login in Settings, quit, and drag Archie to the Trash. Then delete ~/Library/Application Support/com.archie.app, which the Trash leaves.
Two small items of Archie’s stay in Keychain Access on a Mac, under com.archie.app. Delete them there too.
If you set up waking on a Mac, first run sudo /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/archie-wake --uninstall in Terminal.

On Windows, reset first. The uninstaller’s box, “Also remove my Archie data, agents, and settings”, removes Archie’s folders and keeps your saved keys. A scheduled task named Archie\Wake may stay: delete it in Task Scheduler.
Your weekly backups and the Downloads/Archie folder stay where they are.
Every step, and what happens after a plan ends: If You Want to Stop.
words: What happens if I decide to stop using Archie?
You can stop and keep a copy of what you built. Follow these steps in order.
Step one. Save a backup before removing anything. Open Account and find Backups. Archie can save what you built into one file.
You need Archie open to make this backup. It is an ordinary file, with no password on it. Keep it somewhere private and safe, like a tax document.
Step two. If you have a plan, open Account, find Your plan, and select Manage plan to cancel. The plan lasts until the end of the time you paid for.
If you cancel soon after starting, you can email us to ask for a full refund. The refund time limit is below this video.

Step three. Remove your connected accounts on the Connections tab. If you paired a phone, press Disconnect every phone on your agent's Setup tab, under Chat app. That empties its mailbox on our server. For Google or Microsoft, you can also remove access in that company's account settings.
Step four. To erase your agents and saved keys from this computer, open Resetting Archie on the Account page and select Reset Archie. You must type reset to confirm.
If you set up the computer to wake for routines, or want nothing of Archie left on this computer, the list below this video has the last steps.
Step five. Quit Archie and remove the app. On a Mac, drag the app to the Trash. On Windows, open Settings, then Apps, and uninstall Archie. Check the box to remove your Archie data.
Ending a plan does not delete anything from your computer. When your plan has ended, you can also delete your Otian account on our website's account page.
That is the end of Level 3. Next: setting up your agent.

sections.title: You and Archie
sections.lede: Jack introduces Level 4: set up your agent, try your first conversation, and make a morning summary of your day.
words: Let's set up your agent, try your first conversation, and make a morning summary of your day.

sections.title: Setting Up, Clip 1: Choose Your Computer
sections.lede: Step one of setting up: the computer that will run your agent, one you can leave plugged in and awake.
sections.notes_heading: How long setup takes
notes: About five to ten minutes, once. That is our estimate: about five on the free credits, and about ten on an AI account of your own.
How to keep a computer awake while it is plugged in: 0.2.
words: Step one. Choose the computer that will run your agent.
For the best results, use one you can leave plugged in and awake.
For help choosing, watch "Why Your Computer Needs to Stay On" in Level 0.

sections.title: Setting Up, Clip 2: Install Archie
sections.lede: Step two: download Archie from our install page, open it, and what a Mac and Windows show the first time.
sections.notes_heading: Where to download Archie, and what Windows shows
notes: Archie’s download page is otianai.com/archie/install. Type the address into your browser yourself.
Windows shows a box that says Windows protected your PC. The install page shows it and says what to check before you continue.
words: Step two. Type the address of our download page into your browser's address bar. The address is below this video. Download Archie and open the file. On a Mac, drag Archie into the Applications folder, then open it from there.
On a Mac, you may see a message asking whether you want to open Archie. This is a normal check for an app downloaded from the internet.
On Windows, you may see a blue message that says Windows protected your PC.
Select More info. Check that the app name starts with Archie. If it names a different app, stop.
After checking the name, select Run anyway.
The information below this video explains why Windows shows this message.

sections.title: Setting Up, Clip 3: Choose How to Pay for the AI
sections.lede: Step three: the three ways to pay for the AI your agent uses, and what needs an AI account of your own.
sections.notes_heading: Your three choices, and what each costs
notes: Free credits: no card needed. They last 14 days or until they are spent, whichever comes first.
An AI account of your own, with no plan: Archie is free for 20 jobs a day. A job is one piece of work: a reply to you, a routine running, or an email it reacts to.
A plan: $30 a month or $299 a year.
A plan with the AI included: $59 a month or $599 a year, with $25 of Claude use each month.
That $25 refills each paid month and nothing carries over. When it is used up, your agent pauses until the next month, or until you connect an AI account of your own.
Email features and the text watch need an AI account of your own. The free starter credits and the plan with the AI included will not run them.
words: Step three. Choose how to pay for the AI your agent uses.
On a new install, you can start with our free credits. Sign in to claim them. You do not need a payment card.

Alternatively, you can connect your own AI account. Select Set up an AI account at the bottom of Archie's window. With your own account, Archie is free, with a daily job limit. The current limit is below this video.
You can also buy a plan, which takes the daily limit off. The plan with AI included also pays for the AI. Select Get a plan at the bottom of Archie's window.
Email and texts require your own AI account. Right now, they do not work with our free credits or a plan with AI included.

sections.title: Setting Up, Clip 4: Get to Know Your Agent
sections.lede: Step four: your agent’s first questions, the add-ons it may install, and where to read the notes it keeps about you.
words: Step four. Your agent is already set up with a name, a picture, and a few add-ons.

When it asks you whether you want to chat from your phone, select Keep chatting here. Then it asks you a few questions. These include your age, what your days are like, and how you want it to talk to you.
Your agent uses these answers to set itself up. It may also install a few add-ons that fit your needs.
Your agent keeps notes about what it learns on the Knowledge tab. You can read those notes. You can also change your agent's name and personality later.

sections.title: Setting Up, Clip 5: Connect Your Phone
sections.lede: The optional last step: connect Telegram so you can message your agent from your phone, and the claim code that makes you its owner.
sections.notes_heading: The other chat apps
notes: Archie’s guides for the other chat apps are inside the app. Discord and Slack need an app of your own, Matrix needs its own account, and iMessage works on a Mac.
Every chat app Archie works with: 0.8.
words: Step five is optional. Connect a chat app so you can message your agent from your phone. Open your agent's Setup tab and select Chat app. This example uses Telegram.
In Telegram, message BotFather to create a bot for your agent. A bot is the special chat contact you will talk to.
BotFather gives you a token, a code that connects the bot to Archie. Paste that token into Archie.
Archie then shows you a different code, called a claim code. Open the chat with your new bot and send it that code.
Send the claim code to your new bot. BotFather is a different chat.
The first person to send the claim code becomes the owner. Send it yourself right away.
Your phone connection is now set up.

sections.title: Your First Conversation
sections.lede: Three things to try first: a question about your calendar, a change you approve, and a reminder.
words: Your agent is ready. What should you say first?
Try these three things.
First, ask a simple question. For example, "What can I cook with eggs, spinach, and rice?" Your agent answers in the same chat.
Second, give it a task. If your calendar is connected, ask, "What is on my calendar tomorrow?"

Then try, "Move my three o'clock appointment to Thursday." Your agent shows you the change. It waits for your approval before changing the calendar. If it can only read your calendar, it tells you how to let it make changes.

Third, ask for a reminder. For example, "Remind me on the fourteenth to pay the internet bill." Your agent sends you that reminder on that day. If you do not give a time, it picks nine in the morning and tells you.

For bills that repeat each month, add Bills & Subscriptions from the Marketplace. It keeps a list of your bills and reminds you before each one is due. When you pay one, tell your agent, so it can move to the next date.
Use everyday words. Check important details, and tell your agent when something is wrong.
Next: setting up your morning summary.

sections.title: Your First Morning Brief
sections.lede: How to add Morning Brief from the Marketplace, change its time and topics, and avoid getting the same news twice.
words: Would you like a summary of your day each morning?
Morning Brief is a routine you can add from the Marketplace.
It needs the Calendar Manager add-on. Install that first. If you connected your calendar during setup, you already have it.
Open your agent's Routines tab. Select Browse the Marketplace, then install Morning Brief. It starts turned on.
Each morning, it can send your appointments, tasks that are due, upcoming birthdays, and bills due soon. Each section appears only when you have the add-on it needs.
To change the time or the information in the message, open Morning Brief on the Routines tab and select Edit.
Change the schedule under Change the time or days. Change the message topics in What it sends.
You can ask your agent in chat to turn Morning Brief on or off. To change what it includes, use the Routines tab.
Your agent may already send other morning messages, such as Today's Calendar or your task checklist. Turn those off on the Routines tab to avoid getting the same news twice.
Next: what to check when something goes wrong.

sections.title: What to Check When Something Goes Wrong
sections.lede: Four things to check when your agent goes quiet, and how to reach a person if none of them fixes it.
sections.notes_heading: Help, and how fast we answer
notes: Every message gets a reply from a person within one business day, even when the reply is only that we are working on it. That is the sundown rule in the Otian Standard.
More fixes: Is My Agent Broken? To write to us: the contact page.
words: Your agent is quiet, or something does not look right. Here are four things to check.
First, is your computer awake with Archie open?
Your agent stops when the computer sleeps or shuts down, or when you close Archie. Opening Archie starts your agent again, unless you pressed Stop on your agent's page.
Second, did your agent decide that no message was needed?
Sometimes your agent reads an email and leaves it alone. That can be normal. Archie lists those emails and explains why it took no action.
Third, does a connected account need you to sign in again?
Open your agent's Connections tab. If an account says Not opening, select Reconnect and sign in again.
Fourth, have you run out of AI credit or daily jobs?
If your own AI account runs out of credit, your agent tells you in chat and gives you a link to add more. If our free credits run out, it tells you how to keep going.
On the free tier, Archie warns you when you are near the daily job limit. It saves the last few jobs for requests you make directly.
For more help, open our troubleshooting page, Is my agent broken? If you cannot find the answer there, email us. A person reads every message. Our response time is below this video.
That is the end of the course. You are ready to start.
